meta.title: Ondra Tool Gate
meta.description: Tool-schema gating with deterministic intent routing (handbook §8.6, P0). With 96 plugins registering tools, a single prompt is eaten by tool definitions before the conversation starts — the handbook measured 48 commands at 55,154 → 8,433 schema tokens, 84.7% gated away. The mechanism is one call: before each step, run the user's own words through keyword rules, derive the tool families this turn could plausibly need, and hide the rest from that agent's schema view through the upstream seam ctx.tools.restrict — a view change only, never a change to any tool's implementation. Three safety designs: first, the default is observe, which computes but never restricts, so the report can be read before flipping to enforce, the same migration discipline as the organ host's shadow billing; second, when unsure, expose everything — with no rule matched nothing is restricted, because hiding a needed tool makes the model believe it lacks the capability and invent a workaround, which costs far more than tokens; third, a circuit breaker abandons the whole turn when the deny ratio or the remaining tool count crosses its bound. Every recomputation first lifts this plugin's own previous restriction, otherwise the view it reads has already been trimmed by itself, so the allowed set shrinks turn after turn with no error anywhere. run_code is a reserved transport name and can never be hidden. No timers, no tool registration, no prompt fragments, no model calls.
